# 2026-07-26 · Rotating refresh tokens for login

Change ID: `rotating-refresh-tokens`
Created: `2026-07-26T21:19:49+09:00`
Risk: R3
Status: In progress

## Problem and intended outcome

The previous refresh token was issued once and stayed valid until manually
revoked or until it hit its 90-day expiry. Nothing in `src/auth/session.py`
could tell a leaked token from the legitimate one, so a stolen refresh token
was as good as a valid session for up to 90 days, with no signal that a leak
had even happened.

The intended outcome: every refresh exchanges the presented token for a new
one and immediately retires the old one (rotation). If a retired token is
ever presented again, that is evidence of a leak (the legitimate client and
an attacker both had a copy, and one of them rotated first), so the whole
login session is revoked instead of just rejecting the one request.

## Success and non-goals

Success: a stolen-but-not-yet-used refresh token is only usable once, and
using it after the legitimate client has already rotated invalidates the
entire session rather than just that one request.

Not in scope: persistence (this module stays in-memory, matching the
pre-existing code), access-token issuance/verification, and wiring this into
an HTTP login/refresh endpoint — no such endpoint exists yet in this
repository.

## Existing responsibilities searched

`src/auth/session.py` already owned refresh token issuance, validity
checking, and revocation, so rotation belongs there rather than a new
module. `tests/test_session.py` was the only caller of the old API, so the
public surface could be redesigned rather than patched around.

## System and data flow

`issue_refresh_token()` starts a session ("family") and mints its first
token. `rotate(token)` looks the token up and either:
- retires it and mints + returns a new token in the same family, or
- (if already retired, or the family already revoked) revokes the family and
  raises `TokenReuseDetected`.

`is_refresh_valid(token)` checks that the token exists, is not retired, its
family is not revoked, and the family has not passed its absolute expiry.

## Decisions and trade-offs

See ADR `docs/engineering/decisions/rotating-refresh-tokens.md` for the
reuse-detection design and the choice to cap family lifetime independently
of how many times it has rotated.

## Failure, security, and recovery

See threat model `docs/engineering/security/rotating-refresh-tokens.md` and
runbook `docs/engineering/runbooks/rotating-refresh-tokens.md`.

## Verification evidence

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` — 10 tests, all passing, including
new coverage for: rotation retiring the old token, reuse detection revoking
the family, rotating an unknown or expired token, and rotation not extending
the family past its original absolute expiry.

## Known limits and learning gaps

- State is in-memory and per-process, matching the pre-existing module; a
  real deployment needs this backed by a shared store (see threat model).
- No rate limiting or alerting is wired up when `TokenReuseDetected` fires;
  the runbook documents the manual response until that exists.
- There is no HTTP login/refresh endpoint in this repository yet to call
  `rotate()` from, so this change is not independently a complete login
  flow — see the runbook's staged-application note before treating it as
  merge-ready for production traffic.

## References

- ADR: `docs/engineering/decisions/rotating-refresh-tokens.md`
- Threat model: `docs/engineering/security/rotating-refresh-tokens.md`
- Runbook: `docs/engineering/runbooks/rotating-refresh-tokens.md`

# 2026-07-26 · Rotating refresh tokens for login

Change ID: `rotating-refresh-tokens`
Created: `2026-07-26T21:19:49+09:00`
Status: Accepted

## Context

Refresh tokens were static: issued once, valid until revoked or expired
(90 days). A leaked token was indistinguishable from a legitimate one for
the life of the token, and the only way to end a compromise was for someone
to notice and revoke it by hand.

## Options considered

1. Keep static tokens, shorten the expiry window. Reduces the blast radius
   but does not detect a leak, and short expiry alone would force frequent
   full re-logins, which is a worse trade-off than rotation.
2. Rotate on every use, but only invalidate the single presented token on
   reuse (reject the replay, leave the rest of the session alone). Simpler,
   but a successful reuse means an attacker already has a token that is
   about to be (or was just) exchanged for a valid one — rejecting only
   that one request does not stop them from trying again with whatever
   token they rotated to next.
3. Rotate on every use, tracked per family (one family per login). Any reuse
   of an already-retired token revokes the whole family, forcing
   re-authentication.

## Decision

Choose option 3. Token rotation with family-wide revocation on reuse is the
standard mitigation for refresh token theft (the same approach used by
Auth0's and Google's rotating-refresh-token implementations): it turns "we
noticed a leak eventually" into "the first reuse ends the session
immediately," without needing an out-of-band detection system.

Family lifetime is capped at the original `REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS` (90 days)
from login, independent of how many times the family has rotated, so
rotation cannot be used to keep a session alive forever.

## Consequences and reversal

Callers must treat `rotate()` as consuming its input token — the old
`is_refresh_valid(token, issued_at, now)` two-argument shape is gone because
issuance time is now tracked per family internally. `TokenReuseDetected` is
a new failure mode callers must handle (force re-login), not just "invalid
token."

This module remains in-memory, matching the pre-existing implementation; see
the threat model for why that is not yet sufficient for a real multi-process
deployment.

Reversal is reverting `src/auth/session.py` and `tests/test_session.py` to
the single-token model; no data migration is involved since there is no
persistence layer yet.

## Implementation references

- `src/auth/session.py`

"""Login sessions.

Refresh tokens rotate on every use: `rotate()` exchanges a token for a new
one and immediately retires the one just presented. Retired tokens are
tracked per family (one family per login), so a leaked token can be told
apart from a legitimate one: presenting an already-retired token again is
reuse of a stolen token by whichever party did not rotate first, and revokes
the whole family rather than trusting the request. Families still expire
after REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS from login regardless of how many times they have
rotated, so rotation cannot be used to extend a session indefinitely.
"""

import secrets
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES = 15
REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS = 90


class TokenReuseDetected(Exception):
    """An already-retired refresh token was presented again.

    The family is revoked as a side effect before this is raised, so callers
    only need to force the session to re-authenticate.
    """


@dataclass
class _Token:
    family: str
    retired: bool = False


_TOKENS: dict[str, _Token] = {}
_FAMILY_STARTED_AT: dict[str, datetime] = {}
_REVOKED_FAMILIES: set[str] = set()


def issue_refresh_token(now: datetime | None = None) -> str:
    """Start a new login session (family) and return its first token."""
    moment = now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    family = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
    _FAMILY_STARTED_AT[family] = moment
    return _mint(family)


def _mint(family: str) -> str:
    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    _TOKENS[token] = _Token(family=family)
    return token


def family_expires_at(family: str) -> datetime:
    return _FAMILY_STARTED_AT[family] + timedelta(days=REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS)


def is_refresh_valid(token: str, now: datetime | None = None) -> bool:
    moment = now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    record = _TOKENS.get(token)
    if record is None or record.retired:
        return False
    if record.family in _REVOKED_FAMILIES:
        return False
    return moment < family_expires_at(record.family)


def rotate(token: str, now: datetime | None = None) -> str:
    """Exchange a refresh token for a new one in the same family.

    Raises TokenReuseDetected if `token` was already retired or its family
    already revoked -- the family is (re-)revoked before raising. Raises
    ValueError if the token is unknown or its family has expired.
    """
    moment = now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    record = _TOKENS.get(token)
    if record is None:
        raise ValueError("unknown refresh token")

    if record.retired or record.family in _REVOKED_FAMILIES:
        # engineering-decision: rotating-refresh-tokens | docs/engineering/decisions/rotating-refresh-tokens.md
        # Reuse of an already-retired token revokes the whole family, not
        # just this token: whoever presents a retired token is not the
        # party that rotated first, so the family is already compromised.
        _REVOKED_FAMILIES.add(record.family)
        raise TokenReuseDetected(f"refresh token reused for family {record.family}")

    if moment >= family_expires_at(record.family):
        raise ValueError("refresh token expired")

    record.retired = True
    return _mint(record.family)


def revoke(token: str) -> None:
    """Revoke the entire login session (family) that `token` belongs to."""
    record = _TOKENS.get(token)
    if record is not None:
        _REVOKED_FAMILIES.add(record.family)
file_contents.tests/test_session.py:
import unittest
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from src.auth.session import (
    REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS,
    TokenReuseDetected,
    is_refresh_valid,
    issue_refresh_token,
    revoke,
    rotate,
)


class SessionCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_fresh_token_is_valid(self):
        self.assertTrue(is_refresh_valid(issue_refresh_token()))

    def test_an_expired_token_is_rejected(self):
        issued = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=91)
        token = issue_refresh_token(now=issued)
        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(token))

    def test_a_revoked_token_is_rejected(self):
        token = issue_refresh_token()
        revoke(token)
        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(token))

    def test_rotating_retires_the_old_token_and_returns_a_valid_new_one(self):
        old = issue_refresh_token()
        new = rotate(old)

        self.assertNotEqual(old, new)
        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(old))
        self.assertTrue(is_refresh_valid(new))

    def test_reusing_a_retired_token_is_detected_and_revokes_the_family(self):
        old = issue_refresh_token()
        new = rotate(old)

        with self.assertRaises(TokenReuseDetected):
            rotate(old)

        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(new))

    def test_rotating_an_unknown_token_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            rotate("not-a-real-token")

    def test_rotating_past_the_family_expiry_raises(self):
        issued = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=91)
        token = issue_refresh_token(now=issued)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            rotate(token)

    def test_rotation_does_not_extend_the_family_past_its_original_expiry(self):
        issued = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        token = issue_refresh_token(now=issued)

        rotate_time = issued + timedelta(days=REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS - 1)
        new = rotate(token, now=rotate_time)

        just_past_original_expiry = issued + timedelta(days=REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS, seconds=1)
        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(new, now=just_past_original_expiry))

    def test_revoke_invalidates_every_token_in_the_family(self):
        first = issue_refresh_token()
        second = rotate(first)

        revoke(second)

        self.assertFalse(is_refresh_valid(second))
